input.query: A person accused of a cognizable offence carrying up to 3 years imprisonment is threatened with immediate custodial arrest without a magistrate warrant. The police officer has not recorded reasons in writing. What statutory section governs police arrest powers?

items.title: When police may arrest without warrant
items.content: (1) Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits, in the presence of a police officer, a cognizable offence; or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years.

items.documentTitle: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Anr.
items.content:
[ACTIVE PRECEDENT - GOOD LAW]
Case: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Anr.
Citation: (2014) 8 SCC 273
Court: Supreme Court of India
Status: GOOD LAW

Ratio Decidendi:
Police officers shall not automatically arrest accused persons in offences punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years. Mandatory compliance with Section 41 and 41A CrPC (now BNSS Sec 35) is required, including serving notice of appearance and recording reasons for arrest. Magistrates must not authorize detention mechanically.

Summary: Issued mandatory 8-point arrest checklist and prohibited automatic arrests for offences punishable up to 7 years, safeguarding Section 41/41A CrPC (BNSS Sec 35).

Arrest brings humiliation, curtails freedom and casts scars forever. Law has laid down conditions under Section 41 CrPC which must be strictly satisfied before depriving a citizen of his liberty.
